clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Registration system.  Assist in planning a national program 
and developing technical guidance for States, and directing Post Office 
activities concerned with registering persons and families for the pur­
pose of receiving and answering welfare inquiries, and reuniting fam­
ilies in civil defense emergencies. The program shall include:

1. Form s. Procurement, transportation, storage, and distribution 
of safety notification and emergency change of address cards in quan­
tities and localities jointly determined by the Department o f Defense 
and the Post Office Department.

2. Training.  Conduct of training programs for postal employees 
which w ill enable them to operate emergency central postal directories 
and to assist in the operation of a national emergency registration 
system including support of local welfare activities in reuniting 
families.

clauses.label: (b )
clauses.text:
(b ) Damage assessment. Maintain a capability to assess the effects 
of attack on its postal service and resources, both at national and field 
levels, and provide data to the Department of Defense.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Functional Guidance.  The Postmaster General, in carrying 
out the functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the follow­
ing:

clauses.label: (a )
clauses.text:
(a ) Interagency cooperation.  The Postmaster General shall work 
with the heads o f other agencies concerned in the development o f sys­
tems outlined above. He shall utilize to the maximum those capabil­
ities o f other agencies qualified to perform or assist in the performance 
o f assigned functions by contractual or other agreements.

clauses.label: (b )
clauses.text:
(b ) Presidential coordination.  The Director o f the Office of 
Emergency Planning shall advise and assist the President in deter­
mining policy for, and assist him in coordinating the performance of 
functions under this order with the total national preparedness 
program.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Emergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structures required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part o f the continuing activities of the Post Office De­
partment on the basis that it w ill have the responsibility for carrying 
out such programs during an emergency. The Postmaster General 
shall be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under 
this order. Modifications and temporary organizational changes, 
based on emergency conditions, shall be in accordance with policy 
determination by the President.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Em ergency A ctions. Nothing in this order shall be con­
strued as conferring authority under Title I I I  o f the Federal C ivil 
Defense A ct o f 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any 
emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course o f action pre­
pared or developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is reserved 
to the President*

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. Redelegation.  The Postmaster General is hereby authorized 
to redelegate within the Post Office Department the functions herein­
above assigned to him.

Executive Order 11002
ASSIGNING EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS FUNCTIONS TO THE  
POSTMASTER GENERAL
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States, including authority vested in me by Reorganization Plan 
No. 1 of 1958 (72 Stat. 1799), it is hereby ordered as follows:
S e c t io n 1. Scope. The Postmaster General shall assist in the de­
velopment of a national emergency registration system. These plans 
and programs shall be designed to develop a state o f readiness in this 
area with respect to all conditions of national emergency including 
attack upon the United States.
S e c. 2 . Cooperation w ith Departm ent o f Defense.  In  consonance 
with national civil defense plans, programs, and operations of the 
Department o f Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, the Post­
master General shall:
(a) Registration system.  Assist in planning a national program 
and developing technical guidance for States, and directing Post Office 
activities concerned with registering persons and families for the pur­
pose of receiving and answering welfare inquiries, and reuniting fam­
ilies in civil defense emergencies. The program shall include:
1. Form s. Procurement, transportation, storage, and distribution 
of safety notification and emergency change of address cards in quan­
tities and localities jointly determined by the Department o f Defense 
and the Post Office Department.
2. Training.  Conduct of training programs for postal employees 
which w ill enable them to operate emergency central postal directories 
and to assist in the operation of a national emergency registration 
system including support of local welfare activities in reuniting 
families.
(b ) Damage assessment. Maintain a capability to assess the effects 
of attack on its postal service and resources, both at national and field 
levels, and provide data to the Department of Defense.
Sec. 3. Functional Guidance.  The Postmaster General, in carrying 
out the functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the follow­
ing:
(a ) Interagency cooperation.  The Postmaster General shall work 
with the heads o f other agencies concerned in the development o f sys­
tems outlined above. He shall utilize to the maximum those capabil­
ities o f other agencies qualified to perform or assist in the performance 
o f assigned functions by contractual or other agreements.
(b ) Presidential coordination.  The Director o f the Office of 
Emergency Planning shall advise and assist the President in deter­
mining policy for, and assist him in coordinating the performance of 
functions under this order with the total national preparedness 
program.
(c) Emergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structures required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part o f the continuing activities of the Post Office De­
partment on the basis that it w ill have the responsibility for carrying 
out such programs during an emergency. The Postmaster General 
shall be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under 
this order. Modifications and temporary organizational changes, 
based on emergency conditions, shall be in accordance with policy 
determination by the President.
Sec. 4. Em ergency A ctions. Nothing in this order shall be con­
strued as conferring authority under Title I I I  o f the Federal C ivil 
Defense A ct o f 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any 
emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course o f action pre­
pared or developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is reserved 
to the President*
Sec. 5. Redelegation.  The Postmaster General is hereby authorized 
to redelegate within the Post Office Department the functions herein­
above assigned to him.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11002 (signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1539-1540), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 Scope: assistance in a national emergency registration system; Sec. 2 Cooperation with the Department of Defense under EO 10952: (a) registration system (forms, training), (b) damage assessment; Sec. 3 Functional Guidance (a)-(c); Sec. 4 Emergency Actions (no authority to put plans into effect); Sec. 5 Redelegation; Sec. 6 Prior Actions (this order controls over inconsistent prior orders; Emergency Preparedness Order No. 9 revoked). It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (10) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95). Inventory: the dossier's clauses omit the Sec. 1 Scope and some section lead-ins and run some sections together; one override restates the inventory as 6 section clauses with no gap or overlap from Sec. 1 to the end of the Prior Actions section. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog records a 'See' note to EO 10952 (the 1961 civil-defense order the text cites) and the EO 11490 revocation; the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 records only the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds no order naming EO 11002: the hits are an FR Doc number (76-11002, EO 11910), a Public Law section number (sec. 11002 of Pub. L. 101-239, EO 12698), the FR page 90 FR 11002 (EO 14220) and index page numbers in EO 9289 and EO 9602; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. EO 11051 (1962-09-27) sec. 601 does not list it, and none of EO 11087-11095 (February 26, 1963) or EO 11310 (1966) names it. No order amended, suspended or ended any clause between 1962-02-16 and 1969-10-28, so no later event is attached. The Prior Actions section's revocation of an OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order was executed on issuance; revoking this order does not revive it. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions (Part 6 Post Office, Part 7 Interior, Part 8 Agriculture, Part 10 Labor, Part 11 Health, Education, and Welfare, Part 13 Transportation including civil aviation, Part 18 FCC including electromagnetic-radiation control of non-Government stations); Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 11002 in full: it assigned to the Postmaster General national emergency preparedness planning functions (scope, functions, cooperation with the Department of Defense under EO 10952, research, functional guidance), disclaimed any authority to put plans into effect (Emergency Actions), allowed redelegation, and in its Prior Actions section revoked OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 9 (26 F.R. 661-662). EO 11490 Part 6 (Post Office Department) re-assigns the same department's or agency's emergency preparedness functions, adjusted to later changes in organization (sec. 101); that is a new assignment by the consolidating order, not a continuation of EO 11002. Plans and programs developed before 1969-10-28 are completed acts. The revocation of Emergency Preparedness Order No. 9 (26 F.R. 661-662) was executed in 1962 and is not undone by revoking EO 11002. State transferred_or_accrued records the carry-forward of the assignment into EO 11490; no clause of EO 11002 continues. SECTION 501. Functions.

The Attorney General shall perform the following emergency preparedness functions:
